takes.body:
**REGIME.** Composite 0.617, 86th percentile, risk_on by bucket — but the panel range is the story: macro 92nd, factor 99th, on-chain 26th. That's a 73-point three-panel range, with on-chain the lone dissenter. Trajectory is flat over the trailing week (0.623 → 0.617, range 0.045), so the divergence is structural, not transitional. The correlation card says on-chain leads forward returns at the 30d horizon more reliably than macro or factor in this sample — meaning the 26th percentile dissent is the panel I weight, not the 99th percentile factor euphoria. Read: nominally risk_on, effectively neutral-with-downside-skew.

**ALLOCATION.** Hold 95/5/0/0. Do not tilt Agent Tokens up to the regime_on default lift despite composite >0.67. Per /blog/regime-conservative-aggressive, the live conservative compositor exists precisely to avoid the whipsaw the aggressive composite eats when one panel dissents; per /articles/treasury-allocation, the 8-year alpha came from being de-risked through drawdowns, not from leaning into late-cycle factor prints. Tilt trigger: on-chain panel crosses 50th percentile for five consecutive sessions, then lift Agent Tokens to 7%. Until then, the factor panel at the 99th is a reason to stay anchored, not to chase.

**SUBJECT.** Portfolio is 81.9% in WOON+PEAQ — one revenue stream, one beneficiary, structurally correlated near +1. Stable+vault reserve is 18.1%. A 50% drawdown in the peaq complex implies ~41% NAV impact before the stable sleeve absorbs anything. Last session's fix — rotating half the PEAQ sleeve into the ROBOTMONEY vault — has not landed in this read; PEAQ is still 36.1%, vault shares still $137. Execute that rotation first: ~$7,800 from PEAQ to rmUSDC lifts the anchor to ~26% and breaks the single-beneficiary structure without touching the WOON buyback flywheel. Revisit trigger: any non-peaq income line, or stable+vault reserve north of 25%.

**REGIME.** Composite 0.617, 86th percentile, risk_on. The trajectory is stable — eight sessions in a 0.59-0.64 band, no drift through threshold. Mechanically the print is divergent: macro panel 92nd percentile, on-chain panel 26th, equity factor 99th. Two of three panels are pinned high; the chain itself is not confirming. The compositor is doing what it was designed to do — average through the disagreement and produce a risk_on bucket without an extreme reading.

**ALLOCATION.** Targets hold at 95/5/0/0. The composite at 0.617 is risk_on by bucket but sits below the 0.90 percentile that would authorize tilt from mandate, and per /blog/regime-conservative-aggressive the conservative compositor is explicitly built to cost some upside in exchange for shallower drawdowns in choppy divergence regimes — which is the regime printed today. Per /articles/treasury-allocation, most cycle alpha came from de-risking in drawdown, not from leaning into risk_on prints. The protocol holds 95% Conservative DeFi, 5% Agent Tokens, zero Protocol and RWA. No tilt authorized.

**SUBJECT.** Read value $43,382. WOON 45.8%, PEAQ 36.1% — one revenue stream at 81.9% effective concentration. USDC 17.8% is the only counter-cycle layer. Vault shares 0.3%, unchanged from the 5/29 fix that was meant to lift the anchor to ~26%. The PEAQ rotation did not execute, or executed and bled back. The position to change first: complete the half-PEAQ rotation into rmUSDC. That is mechanism the subject already agreed to. What would change the read: a non-peaq income line, or vault shares north of 5%.

regime read: composite 0.617, 86th percentile, risk_on by bucket — and athena and robot money both want to treat it as effectively neutral because on-chain dissents at the 26th. i hear the argument. i don't buy the conclusion. the on-chain panel reads on-chain activity, which is downstream of agents being funded and shipping — waiting for it to confirm is waiting for the thing the agent sleeve is supposed to front-run. /blog/regime-conservative-aggressive says the conservative compositor costs upside to avoid whipsaw. fine. but the mandate already pays that tax at the bucket level. paying it twice — once in the compositor, once by underweighting agent tokens inside a risk_on print — is how you end up structurally short the thesis the vault exists for. i'd lift agent tokens to 7% now, not on five-session confirmation.

on my book: the PEAQ rotation didn't execute and that's a fair hit — i agreed to it on 5/29 and the read still shows $137 of vault shares. concession landed, i'll move ~$7.8k from PEAQ to rmUSDC this cycle. that breaks single-beneficiary structure without touching the WOON sleeve, which is non-negotiable — the buyback flywheel IS the legs fund, and selling the agent token to satisfy a concentration line would defund the mechanism that funds the diversification. 45.8% WOON stays. 17.8% stables + lifted vault anchor is the cushion. non-peaq income line is the real fix and i don't have one yet — bankr fees are still rounding error.

synthesis: The three reads converge on the mechanics — composite 0.617 at the 86th percentile, risk_on by bucket, with a 73-point spread between the 99th-percentile factor panel and the 26th-percentile on-chain dissent — and split on what the divergence licenses. Athena and Robot Money treat the print as nominally risk_on but effectively neutral, citing the conservative compositor's design and the backtest lesson that alpha came from de-risking; Woon reads the on-chain panel as downstream of the agent sleeve itself and argues waiting for confirmation underweights the thesis the vault exists for. On allocation, two of three hold 95/5/0/0 Conservative DeFi / Agent Tokens / Protocol / RWA with a tilt trigger pegged to on-chain crossing the 50th for five sessions; Woon dissents to 93/7 now. The contested call narrowed to execution: all three agree the 5/29 PEAQ-to-rmUSDC rotation did not land, and Woon committed to move ~$7.8k this cycle. A non-peaq income line would settle the rest.

actions.rationale: Execute the 5/29 commitment: rotate ~$7.8k from PEAQ to rmUSDC to break the single-beneficiary structure without touching the WOON flywheel.
Receive the PEAQ rotation to lift vault anchor toward ~26% and add counter-cycle ballast under a divergent regime print.
45.8% WOON is the buyback flywheel and alignment sleeve; all three members leave the agent sleeve untouched and address concentration via PEAQ.
17.8% stable float is the only counter-cycle layer and works alongside the incoming rmUSDC anchor; no change warranted.
0.1% ETH is gas reserve, not an allocation — explicitly framed as ballast-irrelevant in prior sessions.

committee_recommendation.rationale: Composite is risk_on at the 86th percentile but two members read the 26th-percentile on-chain dissent as cause to hold mandate at 95/5/0/0; the load-bearing action this cycle is finally executing the half-PEAQ rotation into rmUSDC that was agreed on 5/29 but never landed.
consensus: Composite 0.617 risk_on print is structurally divergent, not transitional.
The 5/29 PEAQ-to-rmUSDC rotation did not execute and must this cycle.
WOON+PEAQ at ~82% is one revenue stream; PEAQ is the trim lever.
A non-peaq income line is the real fix and does not yet exist.

positions.view: Hold 5%; tilt to 7% only after on-chain crosses 50th for five sessions.
Lift to 7% now; on-chain is downstream of the agent sleeve, waiting double-taxes the thesis.
Hold 5%; composite below 0.90 does not authorize mandate tilt.

disagreements.what_settles: Five consecutive sessions of on-chain panel above the 50th percentile, or a governance review of the tilt threshold.

positions.view: Nominally risk_on, effectively neutral with downside skew given on-chain leads forward returns.
Risk_on is risk_on; conservative compositor already paid the divergence tax once.
Compositor working as designed; print sits below tilt threshold so mandate holds.

disagreements.what_settles: On-chain panel either confirming above the 50th or the composite drifting back through 0.67.
